terminal.description: A shell in your workspace folder. Build Kasimir's stocktake here and run it, so it finds the files in data/.

tasks.title: Read every line of a file
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/stocktake.cpp`, write a function called `readLines` that takes a path as a reference to a `const std::string` and the lines as a reference to a `std::vector<std::string>`, and gives back a `bool`. It opens the file at that path. When the file does not open, it gives back `false` and leaves the lines as they were. Otherwise it adds each line of the file to the end of the lines, in order, without its line end, an empty line as an empty text, and gives back `true`.

Check writes files of its own first, with a blank line in the middle, no line end after the last line, or nothing in them, and calls `readLines` with their paths and a vector that already holds a line. It also hands it the path of a file that is not there.
nextSteps: Write the first line: the path and the lines in, a `bool` back.
Open the file at the path, and ask whether it opened.
Read it a line at a time, with the read itself deciding when to stop, and add each line to the end.
hints: A file that did not open gives no error: reading it simply reads nothing. Only asking the stream tells the two apart.

A stream stands in an `if` or a `while` as true while all is well. A read of a line gives back the stream it read from, so the read itself can be the loop's condition: it is false once a read found nothing more.
The shape is `std::ifstream file(path); if (!file) { return false; } std::string line; while (std::getline(file, line)) { lines.push_back(line); } return true;`.

tasks.title: Add up the drawer
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a function called `totalParts` that takes a stream as a reference to a `std::istream` and gives back an `int`. The stream holds pairs: a part's name, one word, and then its count, a whole number, with spaces or line ends between them, like `data/drawer.txt`. It reads to the end and gives back the counts added up, `0` for an empty stream. When a name is not followed by a whole number, it gives back `-1`.

Check hands `totalParts` string streams of its own, with no file: pairs on one line or on several, a blank line, no line end at the end, a count written as a word, and a name with no count after it.
nextSteps: Write the first line, with the stream as a `std::istream&`.
Read a name, in a way that stops the loop at the end of the stream.
After each name, read its count and ask whether that read worked.
In `main`, open `data/drawer.txt` and hand it to `totalParts`.
hints: Reading a stream works as reading typing did in part 2: a word into a `std::string`, a whole number into an `int`, with spaces and line ends skipped first.

A read stands in an `if` or a `while` as true when it worked. Reading the name can be the loop's condition, and reading the count can be asked about on its own, so a missing or wrong count is told apart from the end.
The shape is `while (in >> name) { if (!(in >> count)) { return -1; } total += count; } return total;`.

tasks.title: Read the bench notes
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a function called `readNotes` that takes a stream as a reference to a `std::istream` and gives back a `std::vector<std::string>`. The first line of the stream holds how many notes follow, as a whole number, like `data/notes.txt`. Each note is the whole of the line after it, spaces kept. It gives back those notes, in order: no more than the first line says, and only the ones the stream really holds.

Check hands `readNotes` string streams of its own: notes with spaces, an empty note, fewer notes than the first line says, more lines than it says, and none.
nextSteps: Write the first line: a `std::istream&` in, a `std::vector<std::string>` back.
Read the number with `>>`, then deal with the rest of that first line.
Read the notes a line at a time, stopping at the number or at the end, whichever comes first.
In `main`, open `data/notes.txt` and print what `readNotes` gives back.
hints: Part 2 met this mix with typing: reading the number stops right before the line end after it, and the next read of a whole line reads that empty rest of the first line.
Skip the rest of the first line before the first note. Then each note is kept only when its read worked: a read at the end of the stream fails and gives nothing new.
The shape is `in >> count; in >> std::ws;` and then a loop whose condition is `static_cast<int>(notes.size()) < count && std::getline(in, note)`.
